name: A.G. BARR p.l.c.
executive_summary: A.G. BARR is a UK branded multi-beverage group (IRN-BRU, Rubicon, Boost, FUNKIN, plus recent acquisitions) delivering consistent margin expansion, cash generation and dividend growth. The quantitative screen rates the name a **buy** (7/22 models; composite 54%; P/E 14.4, P/B 2.0, yield 3.1%, D/E 14%), though an earnings-basis overlay adjusts the signal to **hold** where statutory and adjusted EPS trends diverge. Filings support a value case built on ROCE near 20%, net-cash balance sheet and an 11% dividend increase, against a backdrop of aggressive M&A (Fentimans, Frobishers, Innate-Essence), capex peaking at c.£40m and a £10m H1 supply-chain revenue miss. The central debate is whether management can integrate acquisitions, restore supply reliability and keep ROCE within the 19–21% target while pursuing “double the business” ambition — or whether near-term dilution and execution friction cap re-rating.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, BAG offers a rare combination of **cheapness, quality, dividend and financial health** in one screen: it passes Graham Enterprising, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple and Financial Health, spanning five metric families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) with full data coverage (20/20). Business quality aligns with those screens: FY25/26 adjusted ROCE of 20.4% sits in management’s 19–21% target band; adjusted operating margin reached 14.8% (within the 14–16% range); and net cash at bank was £41.6m post-acquisitions. Revenue has compounded steadily (£400.0m FY23 → £420.4m FY24/25 → £437.3m FY25/26 per final results), driven by value-led pricing and Boost momentum, while IRN-BRU’s revenue share has fallen from 43% to 32% over five years — evidence of deliberate portfolio diversification.

The valuation hook is a mid-teens earnings multiple on a defensive consumer staple with 3.1% yield and dividend cover above 2x (full-year dividend 18.71p on adjusted EPS 44.24p). Management’s Capital Markets Day (June 2025) articulated a credible organic-plus-M&A framework: minimum 4% revenue growth, margin discipline and targeted acquisitions in functional hydration and premium socialising. Timing is neutral (RSI ~35, price slightly below 200-day MA), which suits a phased accumulation rather than momentum chasing. The screen’s earnings-basis caution is material: statutory EPS rose 18.0% while adjusted EPS rose 11.2% in FY25/26, reflecting £3.2m of adjusting items (M&A fees, integration, asset impairment) — growth-dependent models should treat adjusted figures as primary but acknowledge the gap.
financial_review:
**Primary source:** RNS filing bodies. Yahoo (`financials_annual.json`) used only where noted.

**Annual results (FY25/26, 53 weeks to 31 January 2026 — Final Results, 31 March 2026)**

| Metric | FY25/26 | FY24/25 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Revenue | £437.3m | £420.4m | +4.0% |
| Adjusted PBT | £65.8m | £58.5m | +12.5% |
| Adjusted operating margin | 14.8% | 13.6% | +120 bps |
| Adjusted ROCE | 20.4% | 20.8% | −40 bps |
| Adjusted EPS (basic) | 44.24p | 39.77p | +11.2% |
| Statutory PBT | £62.6m | £53.2m | +17.7% |
| Statutory EPS (basic) | 42.27p | 35.81p | +18.0% |
| Cash generated by operations | £64.9m | £57.6m | +12.7% |
| Net cash from operating activities | £51.0m | £48.3m | +5.6% |
| Net cash at bank | £41.6m | £63.9m | −34.9% |
| Full-year dividend | 18.71p | 16.86p | +11.0% |
| Cash capex | £30.4m | £19.2m | +58% |

Growth was **value-led**: overall volume was flat as early-2025 pricing realignment on IRN-BRU and Rubicon temporarily suppressed volumes. Boost delivered double-digit revenue growth; FUNKIN cocktail solutions revenue fell 11% on on-trade weakness. Soft drinks segment revenue was £382.0m (87% of group); largest customer contributed c.£78.2m (~18% of revenue). Balance sheet remained robust: total assets £514.2m, equity £345.6m (including £7.6m non-controlling interest from Innate-Essence), and £40.0m drawn on a £40m RCF at year-end to fund the post-period Fentimans acquisition (£38.4m plus £2.1m director loan settlement).

Three-year revenue trajectory (filings): £400.0m (FY23) → £420.4m (FY24/25) → £437.3m (FY25/26). Adjusted operating margin has rebuilt from 13.6% to 14.8%, entering the stated 14–16% band.

**Interim results (H1 FY25/26, 26 weeks to 26 July 2025 — Interim Results, 30 September 2025)**

| Metric | H1 25/26 | H1 24/25 | Change |
|--------|----------|----------|--------|
| Revenue | £228.1m | £221.3m | +3.1% |
| Adjusted PBT | £35.2m | £29.3m | +20.1% |
| Adjusted operating margin | 15.0% | 13.0% | +200 bps |
| Adjusted EPS (basic) | 24.90p | 19.86p | +25.4% |
| Statutory PBT | £35.2m | £24.9m | +41.4% |
| Net cash at bank | £41.3m | £43.7m | −5.5% |
| Interim dividend | 3.44p | 3.10p | +11.0% |

H1 saw Innate-Essence acquired (£14.7m initial consideration for 50.1%) and Strathmore disposed. No adjusting items in H1; prior-year comparator included £4.4m business-change costs. Management reconfirmed full-year profit expectations at interim.

**Trading updates**

- *Full Year Trading Update* (3 February 2026): revenue c.£437m (+c.4%), adjusted operating margin c.14.7%, acquisitions of Frobishers (£13m) and Fentimans (c.£38m post year-end) announced.
- *Interim Trading Update* (4 August 2026, H1 FY26/27 to 1 August 2026): revenue expected c.£246m (+c.8% vs H1 £228.1m), but c.£10m revenue lost to supply-chain constraints (internal capacity programme and third-party manufacturing). Full-year adjusted PBT guidance maintained (analyst consensus £71.9m cited); H2 double-digit revenue growth anticipated.

**Gaps and fallbacks**

- **H1 FY26/27 interim accounts are not yet filed** (Notice of Results: 29 September 2026); only the 4 August 2026 trading update is available for the current half.
- Companies House annual accounts for 2022–2024 are indexed but **without downloadable body extracts** in this pack.
- **Free cash flow:** FY25/26 FCF of **£20.6m** taken from Yahoo (`financials_annual.json`) — filing shows £51.0m net cash from operating activities and £30.4m capex, implying similar FCF but the filing does not label FCF explicitly.
- Yahoo statutory EPS for FY25/26 (35.81p basic prior year; 42.27p implied current) aligns with filing figures.

**Cash and leverage trend:** The group moved from net cash of £63.9m (Jan 2025) to £41.6m (Jan 2026) after c.£66m of acquisition spend (Innate-Essence, Frobishers, Fentimans). Management targets long-term net debt/EBITDA ≤2.5x and expects capex to peak at c.£40m in FY26/27 before normalising to £30–35m. ROCE is guided towards the **lower end** of 19–21% in FY26/27–FY27/28 as acquisitions integrate.
risks_and_flags:
**Regulatory and industry:** Filings cite evolving UK regulation on sugar content, advertising restrictions and packaging (Deposit Return Scheme legislated for late 2027). These are structural headwinds for traditional soft drinks, partially offset by zero-sugar innovation (IRN-BRU ZERO launch, March 2026 RNS).

**Competitive and customer:** The UK soft drinks market remains “highly competitive” with intensifying promotional activity (interim results). Largest-customer concentration rose to ~18% of revenue (£78.2m); no other customer exceeds 10%, but grocery-channel dependence is a negotiating risk.

**M&A and integration:** FY25/26 adjusting items of £3.2m included M&A and integration costs. Fentimans (c.£40m sales, £1.4m profit at acquisition) and Frobishers are **margin-dilutive** near term; Innate-Essence was loss-making post-acquisition. Contingent consideration on Innate-Essence could reach up to £16m (fair value £2.0m at H1). Integration of Fentimans/Frobishers carries execution risk; Fentimans-related job losses were reported in press (February 2026).

**Operational / supply chain:** The August 2026 trading update disclosed an estimated **£10m H1 revenue impact** from stock availability issues tied to the capacity upgrade programme and third-party manufacturing — a concrete execution miss not visible in screens.

**Governance:** Mark Allen OBE stepped down as Non-Executive Chair (August 2025); Susan Barratt serves as Interim Chair while a successor search proceeds. Dr Rohit Dhawan joined as NED (July 2025). No material governance red flags in filing language, but chair transition adds oversight uncertainty.

**Pension:** Defined-benefit scheme closed to accrual; IAS 19 surplus £0.5m at year-end (down from £6.8m) after further annuity buy-in (c.£41.8m). Remeasurement drove £7.8m OCI expense — accounting volatility, not a funding crisis.

**Liquidity and covenants:** Going-concern basis confirmed in final results and interim accounts. At 31 January 2026 the £40m RCF was fully drawn for Fentimans funding; £20m repaid mid-February 2026. Facility expires **8 May 2026**; management states advanced discussions for replacement financing and cites alternative liquidity options if delayed. Scenario modelling indicates covenant headroom even under severe revenue-loss assumptions.

**Commodity and macro:** Filings flag record aluminium and soft-fruit costs, partly hedged through most of 2026; Middle East conflict noted as an energy-cost risk with no direct revenue exposure.
